abida.title: Abida
abida.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abida.note: A son of Midian, which makes him Abraham's grandson through Keturah, the wife he took after Sarah died. The line is counted among the Arab tribes east and south of Canaan.

abimelech-2.title: Abimelech
abimelech-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
abimelech-2.note: The Philistine king of Gerar. Abraham told him Sarah was his sister and he took her into his household, then gave her back once God warned him in a dream. The same thing played out again later between him and Isaac over Rebekah.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

adbeel.title: Adbeel
adbeel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
adbeel.note: Third of Ishmael's twelve sons. Each of the twelve ended up heading an Arabian tribal confederation.

ahuzzath.title: Ahuzzath
ahuzzath.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ahuzzath.note: He came with Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar, when the king made a treaty with Isaac after the disputes over wells.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

aram-3.title: Aram
aram-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram-3.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

aram-naharaim.title: Aram-naharaim
aram-naharaim.note: Aram of the two rivers, upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's relatives settled there, and the wives of Isaac and Jacob came from it.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

bashemath.title: Bashemath
bashemath.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bashemath.note: One of Esau's wives, in the Genesis lists. The name belongs to more than one of them, and to a daughter of Solomon too.

beer-lahai-roi.title: Beer-lahai-roi
beer-lahai-roi.note: The well of the one who lives and sees me, in the Negev, where the angel of the Lord found Hagar pregnant and running away and spoke to her. Isaac later settled near it.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeri.title: Beeri
beeri.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
beeri.note: Judith's father, a Hittite. She became one of Esau's wives, and the marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

bethuel.title: Bethuel
bethuel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
bethuel.note: Nahor and Milcah's son, Abraham's nephew, and the father of Laban and Rebekah. He shows up in person once, to give his consent when Abraham's servant asked for Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.

bilhah.title: Bilhah
bilhah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bilhah.note: Rachel's maidservant. Laban had given her to Rachel, and when Rachel had no children she gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife. Bilhah bore him Dan and Naphtali.

buz-2.title: Buz
buz-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
buz-2.note: It means contempt. This Buz was the second son of Abraham's brother Nahor, and Elihu, one of Job's counsellors, came from his line.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

chesed.title: Chesed
chesed.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
chesed.note: Nahor's son, one of the descendants of Abraham's brother listed in Genesis 22:22. Some scholars connect the name with the Hebrew word for the Chaldeans, Kasdim.

dan-2.title: Dan
dan-2.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
dan-2.note: Jacob's son by Bilhah, Rachel's servant, and the ancestor of the tribe that carries his name.

dedan-3.title: Dedan
dedan-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
dedan-3.note: One of 3 men called Dedan. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

dinah.title: Dinah
dinah.about: Jacob's daughter living at the time of the Patriarchs
dinah.note: Jacob and Leah's only daughter. After Shechem raped her, Simeon and Levi made the men of his city agree to be circumcised and then killed them all while they were still recovering. On his deathbed Jacob condemned it as reckless cruelty.

dumah.title: Dumah
dumah.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
dumah.note: A son of Ishmael, and the Arabian tribe and region that came from him, usually tied to the oasis of Dumat al-Jandal.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eldaah.title: Eldaah
eldaah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eldaah.note: Youngest of Midian's sons, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, and ancestor of one of the Arabian groups that came from Midian.

elon.title: Elon
elon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
elon.note: A Hittite whose daughter Basemath married Esau; the name means oak.

ephah.title: Ephah
ephah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephah.note: Midian's son and Abraham's grandson through Keturah. His people settled in northern Arabia, and Isaiah pictures the land of Ephah bringing gold and incense to Zion.

epher.title: Epher
epher.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
epher.note: A son of Midian, named in the two lists of Midian's sons and nowhere else.

ephron.title: Ephron
ephron.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephron.note: The Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It was the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned, and Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and their wives were all buried there.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

esau-2.title: Esau
esau-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau-2.note: A man from the patriarchs. Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him 7 times.

esek.title: Esek
esek.note: A well, not a person. Isaac's herdsmen dug it in the valley of Gerar and the herdsmen of Gerar claimed the water, so he called it contention. Sitnah came next, and then Rehoboth, which nobody fought over.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gaham.title: Gaham
gaham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gaham.note: One of the sons Nahor, Abraham's brother, had by his concubine Reumah. Nothing further is recorded.

gerar.title: Gerar
gerar.note: Abraham and Isaac both stayed in this Philistine town in the Negev under a king called Abimelech, and both passed their wives off as sisters out of fear. Isaac reaped a hundredfold there and dug out his father's wells again until quarrels over water moved him on toward Beersheba. Tel Haror is a leading candidate for the site.

hadad-3.title: Hadad
hadad-3.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadad-3.note: A son of Ishmael, in the list of Genesis 25:15. Nothing else is told of him.

hagar.title: Hagar
hagar.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
hagar.note: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham to have the child Sarah could not, and she bore Ishmael. After Isaac came, Sarah had her and the boy sent into the wilderness, and God met her there. She is the only person in Genesis who gives God a name of her own, the God who sees me.

haran.title: Haran
haran.note: Abraham's family stopped and settled here for a while on the way toward Canaan, and Abraham set out again from Haran in Genesis 12:4. The city was likely named after his brother.

havilah-3.title: Havilah
havilah-3.note: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.

hazo.title: Hazo
hazo.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hazo.note: Nahor and Milcah had him, one of the sons who became Aramean clans. Nahor was Abraham's brother.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

heth.title: Heth
heth.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
heth.note: Canaan's son and the father of the Hittites, the people Abraham bought Sarah's burial cave from and the people Uriah, Bathsheba's husband, came from generations later.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

ishbak.title: Ishbak
ishbak.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishbak.note: Abraham had him by Keturah. He is usually taken as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe, but nobody can say which.

ishmael-2.title: Ishmael
ishmael-2.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmael-2.note: Abraham's first son, by Hagar, Sarah's servant. Sarah had given Hagar to Abraham while she was still childless, then wanted mother and son gone after Isaac came. God promised Hagar her son would father a great nation too, though the covenant line ran through Isaac.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jetur.title: Jetur
jetur.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetur.note: He was Ishmael's son, and Chronicles records a war in which Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh beat his descendants.

jidlaph.title: Jidlaph
jidlaph.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jidlaph.note: He was Nahor's son by Milcah, and Nahor was Abraham's brother. Jidlaph is one name in the list of his children and nothing more.

jokshan.title: Jokshan
jokshan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jokshan.note: He was Abraham's son by Keturah, and Sheba and Dedan, names tied to Arabian trading peoples, came from him.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

judith.title: Judith
judith.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
judith.note: Beeri the Hittite's daughter, one of two Hittite wives Esau took at forty, and the marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah. She is usually matched with Oholibamah in the later list in Genesis 36, but the two lists name the wives differently and the match has long been argued over.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

kedemah.title: Kedemah
kedemah.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedemah.note: He was the youngest of Ishmael's twelve sons, and his name means "eastward," which suits sons who settled east of Canaan. Nothing else is recorded about him individually.

kemuel-2.title: Kemuel
kemuel-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
kemuel-2.note: Nahor's son, and so Abraham's nephew.

keturah.title: Keturah
keturah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
keturah.note: The wife Abraham took after Sarah died. Her six sons became Arabian and Midianite peoples, and Abraham sent them away with gifts so Isaac would stand alone as heir.

kirjath-arba.title: Kirjath-arba
kirjath-arba.note: "Arba's city," Hebron's older name, after a great man among the Anakim. Sarah died there and Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah close by to bury her. Joshua gave it to Caleb for the faithful report he brought back as a spy.

laban.title: Laban
laban.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
laban.note: Rebekah's brother and Jacob's uncle, and then his father-in-law twice, after he slipped Leah in where Rachel should have been and got fourteen years of work out of him. He kept changing Jacob's wages as the flocks grew. Jacob finally slipped away with his family, and the two parted under a covenant, not with a fight.

leah.title: Leah
leah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
leah.note: Jacob's first wife, given to him by her father Laban in place of Rachel, and Jacob only found out in the morning. He never loved her the way he loved Rachel. Genesis says God gave her children because she was unloved, and she bore six of the twelve sons, Judah among them.

letushim.title: Letushim
letushim.note: A tribe, not a person. They were one of three groups from Dedan, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, with Asshurim and Leummim, and who they were in history is uncertain.

leummim.title: Leummim
leummim.note: The word means "peoples." It names a group of Arabian tribes from Dedan, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, listed with Asshurim and Letushim.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

luz.title: Luz
luz.note: It was the old Canaanite name of Bethel, where Jacob dreamed of the stairway to heaven, and it hung on in a nearby town after Bethel was renamed.

maachah-9.title: Maachah
maachah-9.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
maachah-9.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

machpelah.title: Machpelah
machpelah.note: The cave near Hebron that Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, with its field, to bury his family. Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah all ended up there. Herod's massive stone enclosure still stands over the traditional site, now a mosque and a synagogue.

mahalath-3.title: Mahalath
mahalath-3.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
mahalath-3.note: Ishmael's daughter, and the wife Esau took to please his parents after his Canaanite wives had upset them. Genesis seems to call her Bashemath as well.

mamre.title: Mamre
mamre.note: Near Hebron, where Abraham settled and built an altar. The three visitors who told him Isaac was coming found him there. Mamre was also the name of an Amorite who stood with Abraham as an ally.

massa.title: Massa
massa.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
massa.note: Ishmael had twelve sons, each the head of an Arabian tribe, and Massa was one. Assyrian records of the eighth century BC name a nomad tribe called Mas'a in the same region, and many scholars take them for his descendants.

medan.title: Medan
medan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
medan.note: Abraham's son by Keturah, and the father of an Arabian tribe counted with Midian east of Canaan.

mibsam.title: Mibsam
mibsam.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
mibsam.note: Ishmael's son, in the lists of Genesis and Chronicles.

midian-2.title: Midian
midian-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
midian-2.note: Abraham's son by Keturah, the man the Midianites traced themselves back to.

milcah.title: Milcah
milcah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
milcah.note: Nahor's wife and Abraham's niece. Through her granddaughter Rebekah, who married Isaac, her branch of the family in Mesopotamia joined back into the main line.

mishma-2.title: Mishma
mishma-2.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
mishma-2.note: One of Ishmael's sons, from whom one of Ishmael's twelve tribes came, a set of twelve to match Israel's.

moriah.title: Moriah
moriah.note: Abraham was told to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him there. Chronicles puts Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Jewish tradition has long taken the two as the same ridge.

nahor.title: Nahor
nahor.about: Abraham's brother living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahor.note: Abraham's brother, Terah's son, who stayed in Mesopotamia when Abraham went to Canaan. His family there gave Isaac a wife, Rebekah, and gave Jacob his uncle and father-in-law, Laban.

naphish.title: Naphish
naphish.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphish.note: Ishmael's son. His people are among the tribes Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh beat in a war that Chronicles records.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebaioth.title: Nebaioth
nebaioth.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
nebaioth.note: Ishmael's firstborn. His descendants were an Arabian trading people, named next to Kedar in Isaiah.

padan.title: Padan
padan.note: Short for Paddan-aram, the country around Haran in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's brother Nahor settled. Rebekah came from there. Jacob ran there years later to get away from Esau.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.

phichol.title: Phichol
phichol.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
phichol.note: He commanded Abimelech's army, and was there when Abimelech made peace with Abraham, and again a generation later with Isaac.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

pildash.title: Pildash
pildash.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
pildash.note: Nahor, Abraham's brother, had eight sons by Milcah, and Pildash was one.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

rebekah.title: Rebekah
rebekah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rebekah.note: Abraham's servant went back to Mesopotamia to find Isaac a wife. He asked for water, and Rebekah offered to water his camels too. That was the sign he had been waiting for.

rehoboth-2.title: Rehoboth
rehoboth-2.note: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

reumah.title: Reumah
reumah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
reumah.note: She was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and bore him four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

sarah.title: Sarah
sarah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
sarah.note: Abraham's wife. She was ninety when Isaac was born, after decades of being unable to have children, and earlier she had doubted the promise could come through her at all.

sheba-5.title: Sheba
sheba-5.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheba-5.note: A man from the patriarchs, named twice across Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

shebah.title: Shebah
shebah.note: Not a person but a well. Isaac's servants dug it, and Genesis 26:33 says it gave Beersheba its name, the well of the oath, or of seven.

shuah.title: Shuah
shuah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shuah.note: One of the sons Abraham had by Keturah. His people settled in Arabia, and Job's friend Bildad the Shuhite probably came from them.

shur.title: Shur
shur.note: The wilderness on Egypt's northeastern frontier, between Egypt and Philistia. The name probably comes from a wall the Egyptians built there against raiders. Hagar ran toward it when Sarah sent her away.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sitnah.title: Sitnah
sitnah.note: The second well Isaac's herdsmen dug in the valley of Gerar. The Philistines there fought over it as they had over the first, so it was called hostility.

syrian-2.title: Syrian
syrian-2.note: In Genesis the word marks the family in Paddan-aram as Arameans, and Deuteronomy 26:5 uses it once more.

tebah.title: Tebah
tebah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tebah.note: Nahor's son by his concubine Reumah, and the first one named. Nahor was Abraham's brother.

tema-2.title: Tema
tema-2.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
tema-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

thahash.title: Thahash
thahash.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
thahash.note: Another of Nahor's sons by Reumah, listed once in Genesis 22:24.

uz-4.title: Uz
uz-4.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
uz-4.note: A man from the patriarchs, and Genesis is the only book that names him.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zilpah.title: Zilpah
zilpah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
zilpah.note: Leah's servant. In the contest between Leah and Rachel for sons she was given to Jacob, and she bore him Gad and Asher.

zimran.title: Zimran
zimran.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zimran.note: Abraham's son by Keturah. He is generally taken as the father of an Arabian tribe that nobody can now identify.

zohar.title: Zohar
zohar.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zohar.note: Two men. One was Ephron's father, the Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah. The other is a son of Simeon in the family lists.
